name: WellDyne
desc:
Customer Care Advocate I | $15-$18/hr | Phone Heavy, No Sales Expectations
Company: WellDyne
Industry: Health Science
What Your Day Will Look Like: You’d answer incoming calls from customers who have questions about their pharmacy benefits, want to place a mail order prescription, or need to check on an order. For many callers you’re the one person they talk to, so you’re the main point of contact. You’d look up their information in several computer systems, explain their benefits, and process or update their prescription orders. If a question is too complex, you’d send it to the right support team. You’d follow set procedures, stay calm and caring when a call gets difficult, and handle a high volume of calls while meeting performance targets.
assessment: Yes, expect an assessment after applying or after initial contact with recruiter
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent. Post-high school or specialized training is a plus.
Required Experience: 1 year of experience in healthcare customer service. Call center experience is a plus.
Preferred Experience: Understanding of HIPAA and privacy rules. Pharmacy or pharmacy benefits experience.
Required Skills:
• Skill with computer systems and moving between several applications
• Excellent verbal and written communication and customer empathy
• Ability to handle high call volumes and meet performance requirements
• Ability to follow processes and procedures
• Ability to handle difficult situations professionally
• Comfort sitting at a computer for long stretches, with some high stress calls
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
• Someone with a year of healthcare customer service experience, like a clinic, hospital, insurance, or pharmacy front desk
• Someone patient and kind who can explain benefits in plain language
• Someone who can move between computer screens while talking with a customer
• Someone comfortable with a steady, high volume of calls and performance goals
Not a Good Fit for:
• Anyone without healthcare customer service experience, since a year is required
• Anyone who dislikes being on the phone most of the day
• Anyone who can’t work Monday through Friday from 11am to 8pm or 12pm to 9pm
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process: 1. Application 2. Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you. 3. If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen. 4. If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview. Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
• Inbound call handling
• Healthcare customer service
• One-call resolution
• High-volume call center experience
• Customer empathy and active listening
• Multi-system navigation
• Accurate order entry and record keeping
• HIPAA and privacy awareness
• De-escalation and difficult calls
• Meeting performance goals
4-5 interview questions for this role:
• Tell us about your healthcare customer service experience and what a typical day looked like.
• How would you explain a pharmacy benefit to a customer who is confused or frustrated?
• Tell us about a time you handled a lot of calls in a day and stayed accurate.
• How do you keep track of customer information while moving between several computer systems?
• What would you do if a customer’s question was too complex for you to answer?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:

Pay: Not stated in posting. Estimated $15 to $18/hr based on general Customer Care Advocate pay, not confirmed by WellDyne. Confirm directly.

Shift: Monday through Friday, 11am to 8pm or 12pm to 9pm. The time zone isn’t stated, confirm directly. Remote training classes run Monday through Friday, 9am to 5:30pm, starting November 2 for the first week.

Benefits: Not itemized in posting. Confirm directly.

Equipment Provided: Not stated in posting.

Felony Friendly?: Case by case.

Drug Test: Certain positions.

Notes: WellDyne is a pharmacy benefits and mail order pharmacy company, and this role is often the customer’s one point of contact for benefit questions and prescription orders. Training is held remotely. The posting says some travel may be required, so ask what that involves. The main requirement is a year of healthcare customer service experience, so ask the recruiter what kinds of jobs count.

Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Customer Care Advocate I → Customer Care Advocate II → Senior Customer Care Advocate → Team Lead.
training: Remote training Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5:30pm, starting November 2 for the first week. Time zone not stated.
